data.body:
Shard C completed its read-only survey of developer comments and embedded prose. It returned twelve candidate groups with exact source anchors and false-positive controls.

- P0. Replace the narrow Python-only comment hygiene policy. The current checker scans Python files under source, tests, and scripts. It permits a historical block when the block contains a ticket or ADR citation. Extend format-aware enforcement to maintained comments, docstrings, presentation strings, prompts, schemas, evaluation specifications, workflow prose, configuration, Terraform, and shell while excluding syntax, vendored content, generated artifacts, frozen evidence, and technical identifiers.
- P0. Correct reconciler prose that still says only the Jira Cloud backend exists, describes Jira Data Center as future work, or presents implemented ACLI and ADF behavior as pending. Current registry decorators, imports, codecs, and Data Center call sites prove both backends and the shared sanitizer contracts.
- P1. Rewrite production comments and docstrings around current behavior, nonobvious constraints, ownership, ordering, safety, and failure semantics. Move module-split history, bug chronology, and former paths to the cited tickets or ADRs.
- P1. Remove the stale claim that the reviewer prompt hygiene test covers 41 prompts. Its current executable glob resolves 58 files. Derive the count or document the invariant without a fixed number.
- P1. Normalize executable prompts, plan-review routing data, evaluation specifications, and schema descriptions without changing criteria meaning, labels, contracts, or scoring intent. Change generated artifacts through their canonical sources.
- P1. Rewrite diagnostics, logs, workflow annotations, shell output, and demonstration strings while preserving structured markers, error codes, field names, and compatibility text.
- P1. Add missing client API docstrings for unlink, tag, untag, archive, and compact. Document parameters, returns, mutation behavior, error mapping, repo_root, and relation behavior from current wrappers and tests.
- P1. Reduce workflow, infrastructure, and configuration comments to current operational rationale. Move measurements, rollout history, former values, and incident narratives to existing tickets. Keep necessary timeout, safety, ordering, secret-handling, and recovery constraints.
- P1. Apply contextual diction remediation across canonical prose sources. Replace filler with the mechanism, source, timing, failure mode, or execution boundary. Do not rewrite identifiers or defined domain terms.
- P2. Rewrite test comments around the protected invariant and failure oracle. Preserve fixture wording when the wording is under test.
- P2. Separate experiment procedure from outcomes. Keep harness docstrings focused on purpose, inputs, outputs, safety, and reproduction. Preserve immutable evidence with provenance and store conclusions in tickets or ADRs.
- P2. Remove ornamental dividers and comments that restate adjacent code only after contextual review. Retain semantic navigation labels and nonobvious rationale.

Measured triage signals include 87 reviewer prompts with 791 em dash candidates and 463 semicolon candidates, 31 evaluation specifications with 263 em dash candidates and 208 semicolon candidates, 62 of 102 schemas with connector candidates in 193 descriptive fields, more than 140 exception messages, 215 logging messages, more than 58 print messages, 4,796 separator candidates, and 633 diction candidates. Counts are not defect totals. Syntax, serialized fixtures, external captures, model outputs, generated files, and technical identifiers require exclusion or source-aware handling. Client-facing argparse help, MCP descriptions, package metadata, scaffold text, and issue templates remain assigned to Shard B. No project files changed.
